mainTopic: Whether a fetus's limb that went out of its mother and came back is permitted by her שחיטה: רב versus רבי יוחנן, and when a fetus counts as born.
overview: This amud asks whether a fetus's leg that came out of its mother and went back in can be permitted by the mother's שחיטה. רב says such a limb stays forbidden. The גמרא defends רב against two ברייתות that seem to permit the limb. It reads 'permitted' as referring to the rest of the fetus or to the מקום חתך, and explains the second word in the פסוק as permitting a קלוט found inside a cow. Then עולא quotes רבי יוחנן, who says the limb itself is permitted, because only a חטאת stays forbidden after leaving its boundary and coming back. A ברייתא, as רבה explains it, compares meat that left its boundary to a טרפה, which can never become permitted again, so עולא is refuted. The גמרא then shows from a פסוק why מעשר שני and ביכורים are different. It brings the ארץ ישראל version of the dispute, where the question is whether a limb can be 'born' by itself, and shows the practical difference between the two versions. The amud ends with two questions about a fetus that came out bit by bit, and a proof attempt that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: what impurity the meat gets
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with a מחלוקת. רבי מאיר says the meat has the טומאה of touching a נבלה. חכמים say it is only like touching a slaughtered טרפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The meat is impure because it touched a נבלה, says רבי מאיר. חכמים say: it touched a slaughtered טרפה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are hearing the last lines of a ברייתא. They cover the case where the fetus's foreleg was still outside when the mother was slaughtered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the leg that was outside is not made kosher by the mother's שחיטה. רבי מאיר says that leg counts as a נבלה, so it makes the meat it touches impure. חכמים say the שחיטה at least saves the leg from נבלה-impurity, so it is only a slaughtered טרפה, which has much lighter impurity.

keyTerms.meaning: Contact with a carcass. This gives real Torah-level טומאה.
A slaughtered טרפה. It is forbidden to eat but does not carry נבלה-impurity.

phrases.english: the flesh is [impure through] contact with a carcass,
phrases.notes: 'The flesh' means the rest of the meat, not the leg that was outside. That leg is what the meat touched.

phrases.english: the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
contact with a slaughtered tereifa.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּשָׂר מַגַּע נְבֵלָה, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the ברייתא that the גמרא began quoting just before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the foreleg was outside at the time of שחיטה, רבי מאיר says the meat has נבלה-contact impurity. חכמים say it only has the impurity of touching a slaughtered טרפה.

steps.title: The first clause seems to permit the limb itself
steps.stepSummary: The first clause says that if the leg came back in before the שחיטה, it is permitted. The גמרא suggests this means the limb itself, which would go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the first part of the ברייתא. If the fetus stuck out its leg and pulled it back in, and only then the mother was slaughtered, it is permitted to eat. Doesn't 'permitted' mean the limb itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the beginning of the same ברייתא to challenge רב. רב holds that a limb which went out stays forbidden even after it returns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first clause the leg went out and came back before the שחיטה, and the ruling is 'permitted.' The simplest reading is that the leg itself is permitted. If so, that directly contradicts רב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In any event, it teaches.' This sets aside the rest of the source and focuses on one line.
The first clause of a ברייתא or משנה.
A limb. Here it means the foreleg that went outside.
'Is it not...?' A rhetorical opener that pushes a reading meant to challenge someone.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two parts of the case. The 'limb' is just the leg that went outside. The 'fetus' is the whole rest of the animal. The whole argument is about which one the word 'permitted' refers to.

phrases.english: In any event, the first clause teaches:
If the fetus extended its foreleg and brought it back,
and afterward one slaughtered its mother –
it is permitted for consumption;
what, is it not referring to the limb?
phrases.notes: If 'permitted' means the leg itself, that goes against רב, who says such a leg stays forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the opening clause of the ברייתא just quoted as the basis for a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a limb which left the mother stays forbidden even after it returns.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'permitted' when the leg came back before the שחיטה. Read simply, that means the leg itself is permitted, against רב.

steps.title: Permitted refers to the fetus, not the limb
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'permitted' in the first clause means the rest of the fetus. The leg itself could still be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is talking about the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by reading the first clause differently. 'Permitted' refers to the body of the fetus.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'permitted' means only the rest of the fetus, the ברייתא says nothing about the leg. So רב can still hold that the leg itself is forbidden, and there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No.' The usual way the גמרא rejects a proposed reading.
A fetus. Here it means the body of the fetus apart from the leg.

phrases.english: No, it is referring to the fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by narrowing what 'permitted' refers to.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the subject of the ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'permitted' meant the limb that went out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Permitted' means the rest of the fetus. The ברייתא is silent about the limb, so רב stands.

steps.title: The last clause makes that answer hard
steps.stepSummary: The last clause says that if the leg came back only after the שחיטה, it is forbidden. If the ברייתא is about the fetus's body, why should the body be forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: If it's about the fetus, look at the last part: if the mother was slaughtered first and only then the leg came back in, it is forbidden to eat. But if we mean the fetus, why would it be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 3 by checking it against the last clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same subject in both clauses. If the first clause's 'permitted' means the fetus, then the last clause's 'forbidden' must also mean the fetus. But the fetus's body was inside the mother when she was slaughtered, so her שחיטה should make it kosher. The answer of step 3 seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If.' Here it tests the answer just given.
'Say the last clause.' This brings the end of the source to test a reading.
'Why?' It asks for the reason behind a ruling that seems not to fit.
Forbidden to eat.

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא often tests a reading by making it work for every clause of a source. A reading that fits the first clause must also fit the last one.

phrases.english: If it is referring to the fetus,
say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: שָׁחַט אֶת אִמּוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ הֶחְזִירוֹ –
phrases.english: if one slaughtered its mother and afterward it brought it back –
phrases.notes: 'It brought it back' means the fetus pulled its leg back inside.

phrases.english: it is prohibited for consumption;
and if it is the fetus, why is it prohibited?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3 using the last clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the ברייתא's rulings refer to the fetus and not to the limb.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The last clause rules 'forbidden.' The fetus's body has no reason to be forbidden, since it was inside during the שחיטה. So the subject there must be the limb, and by the same logic the first clause is about the limb too.

steps.title: The ruling is only about the place of the cut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. The last clause's 'forbidden' refers to the מקום חתך on the fetus's body, not the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב נחמן בר יצחק said elsewhere: the ruling is needed only for the place of the cut. Here too, the ruling is needed only for the place of the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of why the fetus's body would be forbidden. It says the ברייתא only means the small spot on the body where the leg is cut off, the מקום חתך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the leg stayed outside at the time of שחיטה, then the leg is forbidden and so is the spot on the body right at the edge where it was cut. If the leg came back in before the שחיטה, that spot is permitted, but according to רב the leg itself stays forbidden either way. This keeps רב's view safe.

keyTerms.meaning: Like what [so-and-so] said; borrows an explanation given elsewhere
The place of the cut: the spot on the body where the limb is cut off, right at the edge of the womb
Here too; applies the same idea to the current case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the whole fetus becomes forbidden when the leg stays out. Only the leg and the small spot where it is cut off are forbidden. The rest of the fetus stays permitted.

phrases.english: As Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
phrases.notes: His statement is quoted a little later on this page, about אבימי's ברייתא.

phrases.english: It is needed only for the place of the cut;
here too, it is needed only
for the place of the cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: 'forbidden' refers only to the מקום חתך
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The last clause seemed to forbid the whole fetus's body, which makes no sense
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the cut spot is forbidden when the leg stayed out; the leg itself is forbidden in any case, as רב holds

steps.title: אבימי's ברייתא seems to permit the returned hoof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that אבימי brought from בי חוזאי: if the fetus returned a hoof, eat. This sounds like the hoof itself is permitted, against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? When אבימי came from בי חוזאי, he brought a ברייתא with him: If it returned a hoof, eat. If it returned hooves, eat. Doesn't this mean that if it returned a hoof, you may eat that hoof?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב again, this time with a new ברייתא. That ברייתא says that if the fetus brought its hoof back in, you may eat. That sounds like the hoof itself is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב holds that a limb that left the womb stays forbidden even if it went back in. This ברייתא learns from the words פרסה and פרסות in the פסוק that a returned hoof, or returned hooves, may be eaten. The simple reading is that the hooves themselves are allowed, which goes straight against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? Opens a challenge to what was just said
A ברייתא, a tannaitic teaching outside the משנה
A hoof / hooves
Brought back: the fetus pulled its limb back into the womb
Doesn't it mean...? Suggests a reading of a source in order to challenge

phrases.aramaic: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא אֲבִימִי מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי,
phrases.english: Is that so? But when Avimi came from Bei Ḥozai,
he came and brought a baraita with him:
If it returned a hoof, eat;
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק that says both 'hoof' and 'hooves', דברים 14:6.

phrases.english: if it returned hooves, eat.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו הֶחְזִיר פַּרְסָה – אֲכוּל פַּרְסָה?
phrases.english: Doesn't it mean: if it returned a hoof, eat the hoof?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא אֲבִימִי מִבֵּי חוֹזָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense of רב with a new source
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that a limb that left the womb stays forbidden even if it returned
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says 'eat' after the hoof returned, which simply reads as permitting the hoof itself

steps.title: Eat the fetus, not the hoof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'eat' means you may eat the rest of the fetus, not the hoof.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If it returned a hoof, you may eat the fetus.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge the same way as before. 'Eat' refers to the עובר, the fetus's body, and not to the hoof that went out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same move as in step 3. The permission is about the rest of the animal, so the hoof itself can still be forbidden as רב says.

keyTerms.meaning: The fetus

phrases.english: No: if it returned a hoof, eat the fetus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading 'eat' as referring to the fetus, not the limb
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Eat' means eat the fetus; the hoof can still be forbidden

steps.title: Why mention returning if the fetus is permitted anyway?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the ברייתא is about the fetus, why does it say the hoof returned? The fetus is permitted even if it didn't.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it means the fetus, why specifically mention that it returned? Even if it did not return, the fetus would also be permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 7. If the ברייתא is only about the body of the fetus, then bringing the hoof back in should make no difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the fetus is permitted by its mother's שחיטה whether or not a limb is sticking out. So the condition 'it returned' would be pointless. The ברייתא must be teaching something that depends on the hoof returning.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically this? Asks why a detail is mentioned when it seems unnecessary
Even ... also; shows the rule would apply anyway

phrases.english: If it means the fetus, why specifically 'returned'?
Even if it did not return, it would also be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'eat' refers to the fetus
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fetus is permitted whether or not the hoof returned, so the condition 'returned' would teach nothing

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: the returning matters for the place of the cut
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that the returning makes a difference for the מקום חתך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The ruling is needed only for the place of the cut.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains why the ברייתא says 'returned'. It matters for the spot on the body where the hoof would be cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hoof stayed out, the spot right at the edge of the womb is forbidden too. If the hoof came back in, that spot is permitted. So 'returned' does teach something, and the hoof itself can still be forbidden as רב holds. This is the statement that step 5 borrowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for...; limits a ruling to a specific case

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the original source of the מקום חתך idea that the גמרא already used in step 5 to answer the first ברייתא.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
It is needed only for the place of the cut.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case to the מקום חתך
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The condition 'returned' seemed pointless if the ruling is about the fetus
steps.terutzMaskana: Returning the hoof permits the cut spot on the body, while the hoof itself stays forbidden

steps.title: Two פסוקים suggest the limb itself is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learns from two words, hoof and hooves. Perhaps one permits the limb and one permits the מקום חתך, which would go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the ברייתא brings two verses! Doesn't that mean one is for the limb and one is for the place of the cut?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again. The ברייתא uses two sources, 'hoof' and 'hooves'. That suggests two different teachings: one permitting the limb and one permitting the cut spot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא only taught about the מקום חתך, one source would be enough. Having two sources suggests the ברייתא also permits the returned limb itself, which would contradict רב.

keyTerms.meaning: Two verses, here the two words 'hoof' and 'hooves'
He takes it, meaning the ברייתא brings it as its source
A limb
One (of the two)

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי קָא נָסֵיב לַהּ!
phrases.english: But it brings two verses!
phrases.notes: He means the two words in the פסוק, 'hoof' and 'hooves', each used as a separate source.

phrases.english: Doesn't it mean one is for the limb,
and one is for the place of the cut?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא תְּרֵי קְרָאֵי קָא נָסֵיב לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the ברייתא teaches only about the מקום חתך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two sources point to two teachings, and the obvious second teaching is that the limb itself is permitted

steps.title: The second פסוק permits a קלוט inside a cow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that one source teaches the מקום חתך, and the other teaches that a קלוט fetus inside a cow is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. One is for the place of the cut, and one is for a fetus with uncloven hooves found inside a cow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second source a different job that has nothing to do with the limb. It teaches that a fetus without split hooves, found inside a slaughtered cow, is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an animal needs split hooves to be kosher. The extra source teaches that a קלוט found inside a cow is still permitted through its mother's שחיטה. Since both sources now have a use, nothing in the ברייתא permits the returned limb, and רב's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal whose hooves are not split, closed hooves
The insides (womb) of a cow

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא defends רב all the way through: a limb that left the womb stays forbidden even if it came back. Sources that say 'permitted' are read as talking about the rest of the fetus or the מקום חתך. The second source teaches that a קלוט inside a cow is permitted.

phrases.english: No: one is for the place of the cut,
and one is for a fetus with uncloven hooves inside a cow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, חַד לִמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ, וְחַד לְקָלוּט בִּמְעֵי פָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 10
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the second source to a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second source had to be for permitting the limb itself
steps.terutzMaskana: The second source teaches that a קלוט inside a cow is permitted, so רב's view is not contradicted

steps.title: Why a source is needed: רבי שמעון's view on a קלוט
steps.stepSummary: The verse permitting a קלוט fetus inside the cow is needed for רבי שמעון. He forbids a קלוט that was born, but the verse teaches that one still inside its mother is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this source is needed according to רבי שמעון. רבי שמעון said: a קלוט born from a cow is forbidden. That applies only where it came out into the world. But while it is inside its mother, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from step 11. It explains why we need a verse to teach that a קלוט fetus inside a cow is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that a קלוט calf born from a kosher cow is forbidden, because it lacks split hooves. So we need a verse to show that this rule applies only after birth. If the קלוט is still inside the mother when she is slaughtered, it is permitted like the rest of her. This explains why the second word in the ברייתא is not extra, so it cannot be used against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with solid, non-split hooves
Born from a cow (a kosher animal)
Into the open world, meaning it was born
Inside its mother's womb

steps.whatToRemember: The second verse is not extra. One teaches about the cut spot (מקום חתך), and one permits a קלוט while it is still inside its mother. So the ברייתא does not prove anything against רב.

phrases.english: And this is needed according to רבי שמעון,
as רבי שמעון said:
a קלוט born from a cow is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דְּיָצָא לַאֲוִיר הָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: These words apply where it came out into the air of the world,
but if it is inside its mother's womb, it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer of step 11 by explaining whose view needs the קלוט teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the second word in the ברייתא its own job, so it does not prove anything against רב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two words in the ברייתא might permit both the limb and the cut spot, which would go against רב
steps.terutzMaskana: One word teaches the cut spot, and the other permits a קלוט inside the cow according to רבי שמעון

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the limb itself is permitted
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: even the limb that went out of the mother and came back is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: even the limb itself is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion that disagrees with רב. According to רבי יוחנן, even the limb itself is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said that a fetus's limb that went outside the mother stays forbidden, even if it came back in. רבי יוחנן says that once it comes back, it is permitted through the mother's slaughter, just like the rest of the fetus.

keyTerms.meaning: The limb itself (the part that went outside)
Permitted

phrases.english: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן:
And the limb itself is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the attacks on רב were turned away, a disagreeing opinion is brought.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fetus's limb that went out and came back is permitted through the mother's slaughter.

steps.title: רב יהודה objects: רב and שמואל forbid the limb
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה challenges עולא, because רב and שמואל both say the limb itself is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to עולא: But רב and שמואל both say the limb itself is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges עולא's ruling. He points out that two great authorities say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is based on authority. It does not argue from a verse or from logic. רב יהודה was a student of both רב and שמואל, so he is asking how עולא can go against both of them.

keyTerms.meaning: But surely (opens a challenge)
Both of them
Forbidden

phrases.english: רב יהודה said to עולא:
But רב and שמואל
both say that the limb itself is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling just quoted in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling, quoted by עולא, that the limb itself is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two major authorities, רב and שמואל, both rule that the limb is forbidden.

steps.title: עולא shows great respect for רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that רב and שמואל are so great that we would treasure even the dust of their graves. He is about to explain why he still follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Who would give us some of the dust of רב and שמואל, so we could fill our eyes with it!
steps.whatsHappening: עולא first honors רב and שמואל. This sets up his next move, where he explains why he still follows רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא does not deny that רב and שמואל are great. Even so, he feels free to follow רבי יוחנן, and next he gives רבי יוחנן's reason from the verses.

keyTerms.meaning: Dust (here, the dust of their graves)
And we would fill our eyes (a phrase of deep honor)

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not mocking רב and שמואל. This is praise. He still disagrees with them because of רבי יוחנן's source.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן יָהֵיב לַן מֵעַפְרָא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
phrases.english: Who would give us some of the dust of רב and שמואל
phrases.notes: He means the dust of their graves. They were so great that even that would be precious.

phrases.english: so that we could fill our eyes with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן יָהֵיב לַן מֵעַפְרָא דְּרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins עולא's reply to רב יהודה's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts that רב and שמואל are great, then turns to רבי יוחנן's own source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רב and שמואל forbid the limb, nobody should rule against them
steps.terutzMaskana: Even with full respect for them, עולא follows רבי יוחנן, whose source comes next

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's general rule from the verse about טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that at first, everything that leaves its boundary would be included in the verse about flesh in the field, and so would be forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what רבי יוחנן said: everything was included in the verse 'Flesh in the field, a טרפה, you shall not eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: עולא begins רבי יוחנן's proof. First he sets up the general rule, and the next step will show how it is narrowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse 'flesh in the field' teaches that meat which goes out of its proper boundary becomes forbidden. On its own, this would cover everything: a fetus outside the mother, holy meat outside its area, and so on. רבי יוחנן is setting up a general rule that will soon be limited.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in a general rule
Flesh in the field, meaning meat that went outside its boundary
Forbidden meat (here, meat that left its boundary)

phrases.english: Rather, this is what רבי יוחנן said:
Everything was included in
"And flesh in the field, a טרפה, you shall not eat,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַכֹּל הָיוּ בִּכְלַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: עולא moves from showing respect to giving the source behind רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the returned limb is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The verse בשר בשדה טרפה לא תאכלו, read as a general rule that the next step limits

steps.title: Only a חטאת stays forbidden after it comes back
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah singled out a חטאת as forbidden after leaving its boundary and coming back, only a חטאת has this rule. Anything else that comes back is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the verse singled out for you a חטאת that went outside its boundary and came back as forbidden, we see that this rule is only for a חטאת. But with all other things, once they come back, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא finishes רבי יוחנן's proof. The special verse about a חטאת shows that the 'comes back but stays forbidden' rule applies only to a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If everything that came back stayed forbidden, there would be no need for a special verse about a חטאת. Since the Torah singled out a חטאת, the strict rule is limited to it. So a fetus's limb that went out and came back is permitted, against רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Singled out a specific case
A sin offering
Outside its boundary (the area where it may be eaten)
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Once they came back

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's logic: the Torah singled out a חטאת. So the 'went out and came back, still forbidden' rule is only for a חטאת. Everything else, including a fetus's limb, is permitted once it returns.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the disagreement with רב and שמואל about a limb that went out of the mother and came back.

phrases.english: When the verse singled out for you
regarding a חטאת that went outside its boundary
and came back, that it is forbidden,
we see it is a חטאת that the Merciful One singled out,
but with all other things,
once they came back, they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the general rule from step 16 to the case of a חטאת.
steps.raayaObject: That a returned limb, and anything else that returned, is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah's special mention of a חטאת that left its boundary shows the strict rule is limited to it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יוחנן, only a חטאת stays forbidden after going out and coming back. A fetus's limb that came back is permitted.

steps.title: A ברייתא challenges עולא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the word 'טרפה' teaches that meat which left its boundary does not become permitted again, even if it comes back.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: 'Flesh in the field, a טרפה, you shall not eat.' Why does the פסוק say 'טרפה'? Since we see that מעשר שני and ביכורים are permitted again if they went out of their boundary and came back, you might think meat is the same. So the פסוק says 'טרפה'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to go against עולא and רבי יוחנן. The ברייתא says meat that left its boundary stays forbidden even after it comes back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said a limb that went out and came back is permitted, because only a חטאת has the 'stays forbidden' rule. The ברייתא says the word 'טרפה' teaches that all meat that leaves its boundary stays forbidden. It even contrasts this with מעשר שני and ביכורים, which do become permitted again.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, which may only be eaten in ירושלים
First fruits, brought to ירושלים
Boundary, the area where something may be eaten
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
You might have thought

phrases.english: They raised an objection: 'Flesh in the field, a tereifa, you shall not eat.'
phrases.notes: שמות 22:30. 'In the field' means outside the place where it may be eaten.

phrases.english: Why does the verse need to say this?
Since we find with second tithe and first fruits

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיָּצְאוּ חוּץ לִמְחִיצָתָן
phrases.english: that even though they went outside their boundary
and came back, they are permitted,
you might think this too is the same.
So the verse says: 'A tereifa.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of רבי יוחנן in Steps 16-17, that only a חטאת stays forbidden after coming back.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling in the name of רבי יוחנן that a limb that went out and came back is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא learns from 'טרפה' that any meat that leaves its boundary can never become permitted again, not only a חטאת.

steps.title: How does the word 'טרפה' teach this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא learns its rule from the word 'טרפה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the lesson learned from the word?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the ברייתא. It sets up רבה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said 'the פסוק says טרפה' but did not explain how that word proves the meat stays forbidden. The גמרא wants to know the logic behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the lesson? How is it learned?

phrases.english: What is the derivation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the ברייתא in Step 18 gets its rule from the word 'טרפה'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the word 'טרפה' teaches that meat which left its boundary stays forbidden.

steps.title: רבה: meat outside its boundary is like a טרפה
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the meat is compared to a טרפה. A טרפה can never become permitted again, and the same is true of meat that left its boundary.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: It is like a טרפה. Once an animal becomes a טרפה, it can never be permitted again. So too, once meat goes outside its boundary, it can never be permitted again.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the question. The פסוק compares meat that left its boundary to a טרפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טרפה is a fatally wounded animal, and nothing can undo that. By putting the word 'טרפה' next to 'flesh in the field', the פסוק teaches that leaving the boundary is also permanent. This goes against רבי יוחנן's idea that only a חטאת stays forbidden after it comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a fatal wound or defect, which is forbidden to eat
It became a טרפה
It can never again become permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This comparison is the heart of the challenge. It turns 'leaving the boundary' into a permanent status, just like a fatal wound.

phrases.english: Rabba said: It is like a tereifa.
Just as a tereifa, once it is fatally wounded,
can never again be permitted,

phrases.aramaic: אַף בָּשָׂר – כֵּיוָן שֶׁיָּצָא חוּץ לִמְחִיצָתוֹ
phrases.english: so too meat, once it has gone outside its boundary,
can never again be permitted!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק compares meat outside its boundary to a טרפה. Both statuses are permanent and cannot be undone.

steps.title: עולא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a full refutation of עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The refutation of עולא is a conclusive refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the discussion. עולא's ruling is rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא said a limb that went out and came back is permitted. The ברייתא, as רבה explained it, teaches that meat which leaves its boundary never becomes permitted again. Since עולא has no answer, his ruling is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that cannot be answered

steps.whatToRemember: A limb that went out and came back stays forbidden. Meat that leaves its boundary is like a טרפה and can never become permitted again, so עולא in the name of רבי יוחנן is refuted.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'תיובתא' is a final rejection. It means עולא's ruling is overturned, not just questioned.

phrases.english: The refutation of Ulla is a conclusive refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final result from the ברייתא and רבה's explanation.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: עולא's ruling is rejected. Meat that left its boundary stays forbidden even if it comes back.

steps.title: Where do we see that מעשר שני and ביכורים become permitted again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to a line in the ברייתא and asks for the source that מעשר שני and ביכורים are permitted after coming back.
steps.simpleTranslation: The master said: 'Since we find with מעשר שני and ביכורים.' Where do we find this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at a detail of the ברייתא. It asks for the source of the ברייתא's comparison, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumed, without proof, that מעשר שני and ביכורים are permitted again after they leave ירושלים and come back. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק teaches this.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do we find this? What is the source?

phrases.english: The Master said: Since we find
with second tithe and first fruits.
Where do we find this?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: לְפִי שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי וּבִכּוּרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation, the גמרא returns to explain a detail in the ברייתא from Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that מעשר שני and ביכורים are permitted after they leave their boundary and come back.

steps.title: The source: 'You may not eat within your gates'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק only forbids eating מעשר שני and ביכורים outside ירושלים. So if they went out and came back, they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain...' Eating them within your gates is forbidden. But if they went out of their boundary and came back, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. The ban is only on eating these foods outside ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids eating them 'בשעריך', in your towns outside ירושלים. It does not say that leaving ירושלים ruins them for good. So once they are back in ירושלים, they may be eaten again. This is the opposite of meat, which the word 'טרפה' made permanently forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: In your gates, meaning in your towns outside ירושלים
The tithe of your grain, meaning מעשר שני

steps.whatToRemember: For מעשר שני and ביכורים, the ban is only on where you eat them, so they are permitted once they come back. Meat is different: the word 'טרפה' makes leaving the boundary permanent.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'You may not eat within your gates
phrases.notes: דברים 12:17. The same פסוק also lists 'the offering of your hand', which refers to ביכורים.

phrases.english: the tithe of your grain, etc.'
It is within your gates that you may not eat,
but if they went outside their boundary and came back,
they are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק only forbids eating them within your gates, outside ירושלים. Once they are brought back, they may be eaten.

steps.title: The version of the argument taught in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In מערבא they taught: רב holds יש לידה לאברים, and רבי יוחנן holds אין לידה לאברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: In ארץ ישראל they taught it like this. רב says a limb can be 'born' by itself. רבי יוחנן says a limb cannot be 'born' by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן, the way it was taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the version we learned until now, רב forbade the limb because it left its boundary, like a טרפה. Here רב's reason is different: the limb that came out counts as 'born', so the mother's שחיטה no longer covers it. רבי יוחנן says a limb alone is never 'born', so if it is inside at the time of the שחיטה, it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West', meaning ארץ ישראל
A limb can count as 'born' by itself
A limb alone never counts as 'born'

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions agree that רב forbids the limb. They differ only on why: 'it left its boundary' or 'it was born'.

phrases.english: In the West they taught it like this:
phrases.notes: 'The West' is ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.

phrases.english: Rav says: there is birth for limbs,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֵין לֵידָה לְאֵבָרִים.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan says: there is no birth for limbs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of רב's reason, in place of the 'left its boundary' reason discussed earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a limb that came out counts as born. רבי יוחנן: a limb alone is never born.

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between the two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how the two versions of רב's reason lead to different results. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions the limb that came out is forbidden. So the גמרא wants a case where the two reasons give different results.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: He means the two versions of רב's reason: the Babylonian one and the one from ארץ ישראל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the new version differs in practice from the earlier one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical case where 'left its boundary' and 'it was born' give different results.

steps.title: The difference: the small part of the limb still inside
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether to forbid the small part of the limb that stayed inside the womb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is whether to forbid the small part of the limb that is still inside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two versions differ when most of a limb came out and a small part stayed inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the reason is 'birth', a limb that mostly came out counts as born, so the whole limb is forbidden, even the part inside. If the reason is 'it left its boundary', only the part that actually went outside is forbidden. The small part inside stays permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: To forbid
A minority, the smaller part
The part of the limb that is inside

steps.whatToRemember: 'Birth' forbids the whole limb. 'Left its boundary' forbids only the part that went out.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
whether to forbid the minority of the limb that is inside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They differ on whether the small part of the limb still inside is forbidden.

steps.title: Limbs that come out and go back until most of the body has been out
steps.stepSummary: According to אין לידה לאברים, a עובר puts limbs out and pulls them back until most of it has been outside. Is it considered born?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: according to the one who says limbs have no 'birth', what if the עובר put out its leg and pulled it back, then put out its other leg and pulled it back, until most of its body had been out? Do we say most of it has come out? Or, since each part went back in, does it count as back inside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question: when limbs come out one at a time and go back in, do they add up to 'most of the body'?
steps.deeperAnalysis: When most of a עובר comes out, it counts as born, and the mother's שחיטה no longer permits it. The question is whether parts that came out at different times, and each went back in, join together to make that 'most'. One side says most of it has been out. The other side says each part went back, so it is treated as never having left.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked (a real, open question)
A fetus, an unborn animal
Most of it, the majority of its body
Since it went back, it counts as back inside

steps.confusionAlert: This question is only according to רבי יוחנן (אין לידה לאברים). In his view, one limb going out does not make the עובר born.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
According to the one who says there is no birth for limbs,
if the fetus put out its foreleg and brought it back,
and again put out its foreleg and brought it back,
until it completed the majority of it, what is the law?
phrases.notes: All the parts that came out, added together, make up most of the עובר.

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן הָא נְפַק לֵיהּ רוּבָּא,
phrases.english: Do we say: the majority has come out,
or perhaps, since it went back, it went back?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי יוחנן's view from step 24 and asks about a new case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Do parts that came out at different times and went back in join to make 'most of the עובר'?

steps.title: Limbs that come out and are cut off until most of the body has come out
steps.stepSummary: Even if limbs that went back don't count, what if each limb was cut off, until most of the עובר had come out? Is a majority needed all at once?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say that since it went back it counts as back inside, then what if the עובר put out its leg and someone cut it off, then put out the other leg and someone cut it off, until most of it had come out? Do we say most of it has come out? Or do we need most of it to come out all at one time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא builds a second question on top of the first. It asks about a case where the parts never went back in, because each one was cut off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first question, the doubt came from the limbs going back inside. Here the cut-off limbs never came back, so that reason is gone. The only question left is whether 'most of the body' must come out at one time, or whether parts that came out at different times add up.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want to say, meaning: even if the first question is answered this way
And cut it off
All at once, at the same time

steps.whatToRemember: The two questions together ask what makes a עובר 'born': most of its body out at any point, or most of it out at one time?

phrases.english: If you want to say,
since it went back, it went back,
phrases.notes: This is one possible answer to the first question. The גמרא assumes it so it can ask the next question.

phrases.english: if the fetus put out its foreleg and one cut it off,
and again put out its foreleg and one cut it off,
until it completed the majority of it, what is the law?

phrases.aramaic: מִי אָמְרִינַן הָא נָפֵיק לֵיהּ רוּבָּא,
phrases.english: Do we say: the majority has come out,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא רוּבָּא בְּבַת אַחַת בָּעֵינַן?
phrases.english: or perhaps we require a majority all at once?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Assumes one answer to step 27's question and asks a further question built on it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must most of the עובר come out at one time, or do parts that came out separately and never went back add up?

steps.title: Opening a proof attempt for the questions about partial birth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that it is about to bring a source to answer the questions from steps 27-28.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is getting ready to bring a source that may answer the questions just asked about a עובר that came out bit by bit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No proof has been given yet; this line only opens the attempt. The source that follows will be checked to see whether it settles the questions from steps 27-28: whether limbs that went back in count, and whether limbs cut off one at a time add up to a majority.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attempt to answer the questions raised in steps 27 and 28.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a עובר counts as born when most of it came out in stages (limbs going out and back in, or limbs cut off one at a time), according to אין לידה לאברים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Not yet stated. The source, a משנה, is brought on the next amud.
